title: What Are the Indonesian Wedding Traditions You Did Not Know?
audience: Couples in their 30s interested in destination weddings and luxury experiences, AUD 150k+ budget

refresh_of.note: Person: article to refresh. Check legacy slugs and other ranking pages; recommend direct 301s at publish.

notes: REFRESH: the brief reads the old page in full with mcp__Apify__apify--web-fetch; SEO pulls its ranked keywords and status and checks weddedwonderland.com for legacy slugs and other ranking pages. Keep its traditions if sourceable; never reuse wording; drop errors; correct brand terms. Keyword trimmed of its leading space.

Related pages to link, not compete with: /destinations/asia/bali, /destination-packages or /destination-wedding-packages, and /everything-you-need-to-know-when-booking-bulgari-resort-in-bali-for-your-destination-wedding only if natural. No venue pages named, no vendor names.

Diversity: Indonesia has hundreds of ethnic groups and several faiths; Javanese, Balinese Hindu, Sundanese, Minangkabau, Batak and Bugis customs differ; say so once; tie a custom to a group only where sourced; no stereotypes.

Likely customs (brief finalises): Javanese siraman and midodareni; the Javanese panggih (sindur, egg-stepping) as often told unless sourced; the Balinese Hindu wedding (pawiwahan) and purification rites; the Minangkabau suntiang headdress; the Batak ulos; the Bugis uang panai without amounts; the akad nikah in Muslim weddings; kebaya and batik. UNESCO: Indonesian Batik (2009), Indonesian Kris (2008), three genres of traditional dance in Bali (2015), Pantun (2020), kebaya (2024 joint listing) only where UNESCO's own text links them to weddings or ceremonies, page confirmed live and title checked. Indonesian and regional spellings as sources give them.

Destination angle: Bali for Australians. Smartraveller Indonesia checked live, including higher-level areas such as Papua; suggest only areas outside them. Legal steps from official sources only (Smartraveller; the Australian Embassy in Jakarta and Consulate-General in Bali; Indonesian civil registry or religious-affairs pages if readable). Marriage tied to religion under Indonesian law only if an official source says so; same-sex marriage only from an official source. 'Check with the embassy and the registry, including any fees' where unreadable; 'as at November 2026'.

Sources: UNESCO, Indonesia's tourism and culture ministries, museums, Britannica, academic sources. Unsourced becomes 'often told' or is left out; no [[VERIFY]] on 'often told' customs. One honest framing line per section, not repeated 'described as'.
Images: placeholders only; no AI images of people, cultural dress, ceremonies or places; AI only for neutral still lifes (batik cloth) labelled illustrative pending approval.

Speed: WebFetch cannot reach outside sites; Apify web-fetch (parallel) and DataForSEO from the start. Fact-check as 2 parallel batches, 15 min HARD, save after every 3 facts, separate scratch folders; no extra sourcing rounds. Google Drive disconnected; Firecrawl out of credits.
Headings must not contain pasted keywords in brackets.
Do not use 'from first idea to the last dance'; Advisor claims only from brand-facts.md (single point of contact; fee and inclusions in writing); no implied help with legal paperwork.
Person's standards: exactly 4 one-sentence Key takeaways; no prices or amounts; no vendor or venue names; business details deferred; Australian English; no em dashes.
